physics-killer-04.title: Dem throw ball for
physics-killer-04.goal: Apply principles to solve the inquiry problem.
physics-killer-04.material: Dem throw ball for horizontal direction from di edge of cliff wey get height $20\,\mathrm{m}$, and e land for ground below di cliff for point wey get horizontal distance $30\,\mathrm{m}$ from di cliff. Take $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ and ignore air resistance. Which one correctly match, in order, di speed of di ball for di moment e touch ground, and $\theta$ of di angle $\tan\theta$ wey di direction of velocity make with di horizontal for dat time?
physics-killer-04.s.s1.prompt: Dem throw ball for horizontal direction from di edge of cliff wey get height $20\,\mathrm{m}$, and e land for ground below di cliff for point wey get horizontal distance $30\,\mathrm{m}$ from di cliff. Take $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ and ignore air resistance. Which one correctly match, in order, di speed of di ball for di moment e touch ground, and $\theta$ of di angle $\tan\theta$ wey di direction of velocity make with di horizontal for dat time?
physics-killer-04.s.s1.explain: Vertical direction $20=\frac12\cdot10\cdot t^2\Rightarrow t=2\,\mathrm{s}$. Horizontal direction $30=v_0t\Rightarrow v_0=15\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Just before landing $v_y=gt=20\,\mathrm{m/s}$. $v=\sqrt{15^2+20^2}=25\,\mathrm{m/s}$, $\tan\theta=\dfrac{v_y}{v_0}=\dfrac{20}{15}=\dfrac43$. If you add speed as $v_0+gt=35$ na wrong answer ①, if you write $\tan\theta$ upside down e be $\frac34$ (wrong answer ②), and if you use only di vertical component $20\,\mathrm{m/s}$ as speed na wrong answer ④.
